title: Full Hotel Intelligence Investigation

paragraphs: This Full Hotel Intelligence Investigation consolidates the strongest available evidence on ownership, operation, brand status, corporate relationships, people and asset history for Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta. The investigation concludes that the hotel is a company-owned, self-operated GSF asset — not a third-party managed property.

Economic ownership and operating control sit with Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: HOTEL). Primary filings support 100% ownership after the 2014 acquisition of Chartwell's remaining stake, with consolidation in GSF's company-owned segment across 4Q24, 1Q25, and 2Q25 disclosures.

The property vehicle identified in related-party filings is Inmobiliaria en Hotelería Vallarta Santa Fe, S. de R.L. de C.V. (IHVSF). IHVSF appears as counterparty to (a) a 2013 federal-zone services contract under concession DZF-334/89 and (b) a 2011 lease-with-purchase-option covering event-hall parcels tied to Hotel Hilton Vallarta — both linking IHVSF to this physical asset.

Public-company beneficial shareholders exceeding 10% of GSF capital are disclosed in the 2025 Annual Report: Carlos Gerardo Ancira Elizondo (29.3585%), Jorge M. Pérez (29.3233%), Pablo Villanueva Martínez (10.5001%), and Hector Fabian Gomez Sainz Garcia (10.0547%). Ancira is designated as the sole shareholder exercising control or command power. These are public-company control findings, not deed-level natural-person title ownership of the PropCo.

Operator posture is owner-operator under GSF's proprietary Krystal Grand brand. The hotel is also distributed via Hyatt Inclusive Collection as an independent property — a distribution/marketing arrangement rather than a current franchise/management agreement. Any intercompany management agreement between PropCo and operating subsidiary is not publicly disclosed.

Current public branding remains Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta. Brand history runs Hilton (2012) → Krystal Altitude → Krystal Grand. Later brand research resolves that the February 2024 Breathless Puerto Vallarta announcement is a same-asset conversion/rebranding of this hotel — not a separate adjacent or greenfield project.

At the same time, conversion is not shown as completed. 2Q25 still lists Krystal Grand; September 2026 operating checks (TripAdvisor/Google) still show Krystal Grand; Hyatt's active Breathless Mexico destinations do not list Puerto Vallarta. The conversion appears materially delayed and may be postponed or cancelled.

Asset history includes 2011 development with Chartwell, 2012 Hilton opening (~259 rooms), 2014 full GSF ownership, 2016–2018 Hacienda expansion to 451 rooms (259 Resort + 192 Hacienda), all-inclusive Grand Tourism positioning, and extensive amenity inventory.

Organization intelligence positions GSF as a dual-model Mexican public hotel company (~25 hotels / 6,215 rooms as of 2Q25; 15 company-owned; 10 third-party managed), with IR and CFO contact channels published and a multi-brand partner set spanning Hyatt, Hilton, Accor, and Inclusive Collection brands.

Decision relevance concentrates with Francisco Zinser (strategically relevant for brand/partnership strategy and Breathless announcement spokesperson), Francisco Medina (CEO), Carlos Ancira (board president / control shareholder), Enrique Martínez (CFO), and Hyatt counterparts Javier Coll and Camilo Bolaños. Property GM is only partially identified ("Luis A, Director General"). Titles establish strategic relevance; decision/signing authority is not independently established.

Principal open issues now concern land tenure (fee simple vs ground lease), deed/notarial signatories, natural-person PropCo UBO beyond consolidated ownership, full GM identity, and an updated Breathless conversion timeline. Earlier gaps on PropCo identity and >10% beneficial shareholders are resolved by later filings and should not be restated as current unknowns.

blocks.text: OWNERSHIP CHAIN — Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta
Key Finding: GSF owns 100% of this hotel — it is NOT a third-party managed property

paragraphs: Claim: Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta (451 rooms, Av. de las Garzas 136, Zona Hotelera, Puerto Vallarta) is 100% owned by Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: HOTEL).

rows: Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta (451 rooms, Av. de las Garzas 136, Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco)
GSF corporate site, official hotel website, Travel Weekly
Inmobiliaria en Hotelería Vallarta Santa Fe, S. de R. L. de C. V. ("IHVSF")

GSF 2025 Annual Report (BMV XBRL), "Operaciones con personas relacionadas" section (p. 110-111). IHVSF is named as the counterparty in: (a) a services contract with Promotora Turística Mexicana for federal-zone services under concession DZF-334/89 (signed Sep 27, 2013), and (b) a lease with purchase option on two properties totaling 1,076.64 sqm "in which event halls of Hotel Hilton Vallarta are currently located" (signed Jul 8, 2011). Both contracts tie IHVSF directly to the Hilton/Krystal Grand Vallarta physical asset. IHVSF's legal address matches GSF's corporate HQ (Av. Juan Salvador Agraz 65, Piso 20, Santa Fe Cuajimalpa, Mexico City).
Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: HOTEL) — 100% owner. GSF holds IHVSF as a 100%-owned subsidiary.

4Q24 report: "Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta — 100% Ownership"; 1Q25 and 2Q25 reports confirm same at 100% consolidation. The 2025 Annual Report lists "Krystal Grand Vallarta" among consolidated Company-owned hotels. GSF describes itself as a holding company whose principal assets are shares of its subsidiaries. IHVSF's address is GSF's corporate HQ — consistent with being a consolidated subsidiary.

Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. is itself the publicly traded parent. Historical PE backing: Nexxus Capital, Walton Street Capital, Grupo Chartwell. Nexxus distributed its 19.1% stake to its limited partners on Mar 25, 2018 — it is no longer a significant shareholder. Walton Street Capital merged into GSF at IPO (Sep 2014).
GSF 2025 Annual Report: Nexxus distribution described on p. 69. GSF is a self-administered public company — no external manager.

CONFIRMED: (1) Carlos Gerardo Ancira Elizondo — 29.3585% (directly and through Hotelera Chicome, HCI Real Estate Management, and Circum Comercial, S.A. de C.V.); (2) Jorge M. Pérez — 29.3233% (through Jorge Pérez JMP Enterprise Holdings LLLP and Jorge Manuel Pérez 2018 Family Trust); (3) Pablo Villanueva Martínez — 10.5001%; (4) Hector Fabian Gomez Sainz Garcia — 10.0547%

GSF 2025 Annual Report: "Accionistas Beneficiarios de más del 10% del capital social" (p. 128) and "Accionistas que ejercen influencia significativa / control o poder de mando" (p. 126). Carlos Ancira is designated as the sole shareholder exercising control or command power. Jorge M. Pérez is "JP" Pérez — President of Related Group of Florida, a major Miami-based real estate developer.

paragraphs: Precision note: These are public-company beneficial shareholders / control of Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. They are not independently verified as natural-person deed holders of the hotel PropCo title. Natural-person UBO of IHVSF beyond the consolidated subsidiary relationship remains not verified from deed/notarial sources.

Resolved research question (RESOLVED): The PropCo entity is now CONFIRMED as Inmobiliaria en Hotelería Vallarta Santa Fe, S. de R. L. de C. V. ("IHVSF"), named in GSF 2025 Annual Report related-party transactions section.

Resolved research question (RESOLVED): Controlling shareholders (>10%) now CONFIRMED from GSF 2025 Annual Report "Accionistas Beneficiarios" section: Carlos Gerardo Ancira Elizondo (29.3585%), Jorge M. Pérez (29.3233%), Pablo Villanueva Martínez (10.5001%), Hector Fabian Gomez Sainz Garcia (10.0547%). Carlos Ancira is the sole shareholder exercising control/command power.

Early evidence suggested a third-party management structure; subsequent primary filings established that the hotel is company-owned and self-operated. The 4Q24 and 1Q25 earnings reports definitively show this hotel is 100% owned by GSF — it appears in the "Company-owned" segment, NOT the "Third-party hotels under management" segment. This is a major correction to the research premise.

blocks.text: Important Findings from 2024/2023 BMV Annual Reports

items: Original Development: The Hilton Puerto Vallarta hotel was developed jointly by GSF and Grupo Chartwell. Construction began July 2011, and the hotel opened October 2012 with 259 rooms. This was GSF's first ground-up development.

2014 GSF acquires 50% from Grupo Chartwell: In August 2014, GSF agreed to acquire the remaining 50% of the Hilton Puerto Vallarta from Grupo Chartwell. After the IPO (Sept 2014), GSF owned 100% directly or indirectly.

2016 Hacienda expansion acquisition: In October 2016, GSF acquired adjacent real estate (54 private-use hotel units and undeveloped land, approximately 15,100 sqm) for EUA$12.0 million (Ps. 224 million). An additional Ps. 296 million was invested, totaling Ps. 520 million. The Hacienda opened April 2018 with 192 suites.
2022 Brand change: The hotel changed from Hilton to Krystal Altitude in October 2022, then subsequently to Krystal Grand.
2024 Brand change announcement: The Feb 2024 announcement plans conversion to Breathless Puerto Vallarta Resort & Spa.

blocks.text: Important Distinction: Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta is NOT GSF-Owned

paragraphs: The 530-room Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta (Av. Francisco Medina Ascencio) is owned by Grupo Chartwell and only operated by GSF under a management contract. The 2024 Annual Report states: "Actualmente los hoteles Krystal Resort Cancun, Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta y Krystal Resort Ixtapa pertenecen a Grupo Chartwell y son operados por GHSF y no consolidan en Estados Financieros." The operating contracts were signed Feb 2010 and renewed Feb 2020 through 2030. This is a separate asset from Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta.

Key Finding: Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta is both 100% owned AND operated by Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe. It is NOT a third-party management contract — GSF owns the asset and operates it under its own proprietary Krystal Grand brand.

blocks.text: 2Q25 Status Update (as of June 30, 2025 — filed July 24, 2025)

items: Hotel still listed as "Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta" — 100% ownership, 451 rooms, Resort, Grand Tourism, in GSF's 2Q25 portfolio table (filed July 24, 2025).

No Breathless mention in 2Q25 report: Francisco Zinser's Executive VP commentary in the 2Q25 report makes no reference to the Breathless conversion — the commentary focuses on occupancy records and RevPAR growth.

2025 Annual Report (filed ~Apr 2026): Still refers to the asset as "Hotel Hilton Vallarta" in the related-party transactions section (p. 110-111), dated Dec 2025. This suggests the conversion may have been delayed significantly.
GSF total portfolio: 25 properties (6,215 rooms) as of 2Q25, down from 26 (6,258 rooms) due to removal of SLS Cancun.

CONTESTED → NOW SUPPORTED: The Census affiliation listing Breathless Resorts & Spas is now understood as reflecting the ANNOUNCED conversion — the hotel was to become a Breathless-branded property. However, as of the latest public filing (2Q25, July 2025), the hotel was still operating as Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta.

CURRENT brand status: Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta — the hotel continues to operate under this name. The original Q2 2025 Breathless conversion target has likely been delayed. Monitor GSF 3Q25, 4Q25, and 1Q26 reports for status updates.

CONFIRMED: Hotel still operating as Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta. TripAdvisor reviews posted Sep 1-3, 2026 reference "Grand Crystal" and "Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta." Google Maps lists the hotel as "Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta" — 5-star, actively bookable, 7,533 reviews (4.1★).

Hyatt Breathless page: The Hyatt Inclusive Collection Breathless Mexico destinations page (hyattinclusivecollection.com/en/resorts-hotels/breathless/destinations/mexico/) does not list Puerto Vallarta among active Breathless locations. Currently active Breathless resorts are in Cancun (Riviera Cancun, Soul Cancun) and Cabo San Lucas.

GM Identified: A TripAdvisor owner response from Feb 2025 is signed by "Luis A, Director General" — strongly suggesting the General Manager is Luis A. (possibly Luis Alberto or similar). This is partial — surname not yet confirmed.
Original timeline: Announced Feb 14, 2024; target opening Q2 2025 (April 2025 per Hyatt Previews 2025 Resort Openings)

As of Sep 2026: Over 17 months past original target with no public evidence of conversion. The hotel continues to operate under Krystal Grand branding with no evidence of dual-branding, renovation, or Breathless signage.
GSF silence: No mentions of Breathless in GSF 1Q25, 2Q25, or 3Q25 quarterly reports. Francisco Zinser's last public mention was in the 4Q23 (Feb 2024) report.
Hyatt silence: Hyatt's 2025 resort preview mentioned the opening but no subsequent update. The Breathless Puerto Vallarta page on hyatt.com is not active for reservations.

Assessment: The conversion appears either significantly delayed or possibly cancelled. Commercial implications: if conversion is on hold, GSF may be open to alternative brand partnerships; if delayed, timing intelligence is critical for outreach.
Exact effective date of the Breathless rebranding — originally announced as "second quarter of 2025" but not achieved. New target unknown.

The hotel's official contact email is reservations.kgapv@krystal.hotels.com and phone +52 (322) 176 11 76.

This chapter consolidates transaction and capital events from ownership and property-vehicle evidence, including development, Chartwell buyout, IPO-era ownership consolidation, Hacienda expansion investment, related-party leases/contracts, and brand-change announcements.

Precision note: These are public-company beneficial shareholders / control of Grupo Hotelero Santa Fe, S.A.B. de C.V. They are not independently verified as natural-person deed holders of the hotel PropCo title. Natural-person UBO of IHVSF beyond the consolidated subsidiary relationship remains not verified from deed/notarial sources.

Resolved research question (RESOLVED): The PropCo entity is now CONFIRMED as Inmobiliaria en Hotelería Vallarta Santa Fe, S. de R. L. de C. V. ("IHVSF"), named in GSF 2025 Annual Report related-party transactions section.

items: Original Development: The Hilton Puerto Vallarta hotel was developed jointly by GSF and Grupo Chartwell. Construction began July 2011, and the hotel opened October 2012 with 259 rooms. This was GSF's first ground-up development.

2014 GSF acquires 50% from Grupo Chartwell: In August 2014, GSF agreed to acquire the remaining 50% of the Hilton Puerto Vallarta from Grupo Chartwell. After the IPO (Sept 2014), GSF owned 100% directly or indirectly.

2016 Hacienda expansion acquisition: In October 2016, GSF acquired adjacent real estate (54 private-use hotel units and undeveloped land, approximately 15,100 sqm) for EUA$12.0 million (Ps. 224 million). An additional Ps. 296 million was invested, totaling Ps. 520 million. The Hacienda opened April 2018 with 192 suites.
2022 Brand change: The hotel changed from Hilton to Krystal Altitude in October 2022, then subsequently to Krystal Grand.
2024 Brand change announcement: The Feb 2024 announcement plans conversion to Breathless Puerto Vallarta Resort & Spa.

blocks.text: Key Subsidiaries Named in Annual Reports (Updated per 2025 Annual Report)
Important Distinction: Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta is NOT GSF-Owned

paragraphs: The 530-room Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta (Av. Francisco Medina Ascencio) is owned by Grupo Chartwell and only operated by GSF under a management contract. The 2024 Annual Report states: "Actualmente los hoteles Krystal Resort Cancun, Krystal Resort Puerto Vallarta y Krystal Resort Ixtapa pertenecen a Grupo Chartwell y son operados por GHSF y no consolidan en Estados Financieros." The operating contracts were signed Feb 2010 and renewed Feb 2020 through 2030. This is a separate asset from Krystal Grand Puerto Vallarta.

Francisco Zinser Cieslik (Executive Vice President, GSF) is a strategically relevant executive for brand partnership strategy at GSF. He publicly announced the Breathless conversion and has been a visible architect of GSF's multi-brand strategy — building relationships with Hyatt, Hilton, AMResorts, and Accor. For commercial outreach related to this asset, Zinser is a likely relationship holder on the GSF side. Decision/signing authority is not independently established from titles alone.

On the Hyatt side, Camilo Bolaños (SVP Development, LATAM & Caribbean) is the publicly evidenced brand-development contact for GSF in the Feb 2024 announcement, described as involved across multiple GSF-Hyatt collaborations. That does not independently establish franchise or legal signing authority.

items: IR channel (low friction): Rodrigo Ancira (inversionistas@gsf-hotels.com, +52 55 5261 4508) or Maximilian Zimmermann (mzimmermann@gsf-hotels.com) for corporate inquiries. These are the publicly listed IR contacts and the lowest-friction entry point. Note the temporal title conflict between IR surfaces (see People section).
CFO channel: Enrique Martínez (emartinez@gsf-hotels.com, +52 55 5261 0807) for financial/property-level discussions.

Executive channel: Francisco Zinser is strategically relevant for brand partnerships; introductions through IR or Hyatt relationship channels are typically the practical path. Warm-introduction requirements are not independently proven.
Property channel: Hotel contact is reservations.kgapv@krystal.hotels.com, +52 (322) 176 11 76. GM surname remains only partially identified ("Luis A, Director General").

Announced Breathless conversion (same asset), not completed: Research resolved that Breathless Puerto Vallarta is the announced conversion/rebranding of this hotel. As of September 2026 operating checks, conversion is not completed and appears materially delayed / possibly postponed. Brand-transition uncertainty remains a commercial intelligence window.

GSF-Hyatt strategic relationship: This is GSF's 6th Hyatt property collaboration context, deepening an important partnership. Whether conversion proceeds, delays, or is abandoned affects future GSF-Hyatt collaboration signals.

451-room scale: At 451 rooms (Grand Tourism category), this is a significant resort asset in GSF's portfolio. A Breathless adults-only repositioning would represent a fundamental customer-base change.
Puerto Vallarta market: GSF has three properties in the PV market (this one, Krystal Resort PV, Krystal Grand Nuevo Vallarta). PV is a strategic resort market for GSF.
GSF operates ~25 hotels / ~6,215 rooms across Mexico (2Q25) — any commercial relationship with GSF potentially extends across the portfolio.
GSF is already a multi-brand operator (Hyatt, Hilton, Accor, AMResorts) — they actively manage brand partnerships and are not captive to any single brand family.

GSF's pattern of converting owned assets across brands (Hilton Puerto Vallarta → Krystal Altitude → Krystal Grand → announced Breathless) demonstrates active asset management and periodic brand evaluation.

Conversion status monitoring: Originally targeted Q2 2025 but appears delayed. Monitoring official Breathless launch updates, Hyatt destination pages, and GSF quarterly commentary provides engagement windows.
Quarterly earnings: GSF reports quarterly (Feb, Apr, Jul, Oct) — natural intelligence-gathering windows for portfolio updates.
BMV annual report: The annual XBRL filing (~April each year) remains the best opportunity for subsidiary-level and related-party disclosures.
